desc:
A block is a square of k x k consecutive cells of the grid matrix. Return the largest possible sum of the cells of a block.

matrix = [[1, 2, 3],
          [4, 5, 6],
          [7, 8, 9]], k = 2
blocks: 12, 16, 24, 28
result = 28
hints: There are at most (R - k + 1) * (C - k + 1) blocks. Summing each from scratch costs k<sup>2</sup> per block, which gets slow for large k.
Neighbouring blocks overlap almost completely. A table of rectangle sums from the top-left corner lets you get any block sum in constant time.
With P[i][j] = sum of the top-left i x j rectangle, the block with top-left cell (i, j) has sum P[i+k][j+k] - P[i][j+k] - P[i+k][j] + P[i][j]. Take the maximum over all positions.
editorial: Build the 2-D prefix table P of size (R + 1) x (C + 1) once, using P[i][j] = matrix[i-1][j-1] + P[i-1][j] + P[i][j-1] - P[i-1][j-1].
Then slide the block over every top-left position (i, j) with 0 ≤ i ≤ R-k and 0 ≤ j ≤ C-k, evaluate its sum with four lookups, and keep the maximum. Time O(R * C), space O(R * C).
Negative cells are fine: the maximum is taken over all blocks, so no special handling is needed. The largest possible magnitude is 3,600 * 1,000, comfortably inside 32 bits.
